title: Market Response Models: Econometric and Time Series Analysis
author_source: Dominique M. Hanssens, Leonard J. Parsons, Randall L. Schultz, 2001, 2nd edition, Kluwer/Springer (International Series in Quantitative Marketing 12), book
note: Still the reference text for aggregate response modelling: sales response functions, lag structures (Koyck and adstock), elasticities, time-series methods (persistence, VAR) and how response models feed allocation decisions. Dense but exact; most Google and Meta MMM papers cite it.
course_use: Session 1 reading (chapters on response model specification and lag structures) and session 3 (decision models and allocation). Paywalled; library copy or e-book, roughly EUR 150 to 200 new.

title: Modeling Markets: Analyzing Marketing Phenomena and Improving Marketing Decision Making
author_source: Peter S. H. Leeflang, Jaap E. Wieringa, Tammo H. A. Bijmolt, Koen H. Pauwels, 2015, Springer (International Series in Quantitative Marketing), book, DOI 10.1007/978-1-4939-2086-0 (verified via chapter link)
note: The most teachable modern textbook on marketing models: specification, estimation, validation and use, with a full chapter of worked aggregate-demand models (chapter 7, "Examples of models for aggregate demand"). European authors, European examples.
course_use: Session 1 core reading (chapters on model building and aggregate demand), session 4 for validation chapters. WU library likely has Springer access; otherwise paywalled.

title: Advanced Methods for Modeling Markets
author_source: Peter S. H. Leeflang, Jaap E. Wieringa, Tammo H. A. Bijmolt, Koen H. Pauwels (eds), 2017, Springer, edited book, DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-53469-5 (verified)
note: Companion volume with chapters on Bayesian analysis, time-series models, endogeneity, structural models and mixture models, each written by specialists. The Bayesian and endogeneity chapters are the academic bridge to Meridian and PyMC-Marketing.
course_use: Background for session 2 (Bayesian chapter) and session 4 (endogeneity, time series). Paywalled; Springer access needed.

title: Python for Marketing Research and Analytics
author_source: Jason S. Schwarz, Chris Chapman, Elea McDonnell Feit, 2020, Springer, textbook with code, DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-49720-0 (verified); code at https://github.com/python-marketing-research/python-marketing-research-1ed (verified)
note: The only mainstream marketing analytics textbook written in Python (pandas, statsmodels, scikit-learn), by two Google researchers and a Penn professor. Covers data handling, linear models, model interpretation and segmentation with marketing data; no MMM chapter, but it sets the coding baseline. The R twin is Chapman and Feit, R for Marketing Research and Analytics, 2nd ed., 2019, Springer, with free slides and exercises at https://r-marketing.r-forge.r-project.org/ (verified).
course_use: Pre-course or session 1 lab warm-up (chapters on data wrangling and linear models). Paywalled book; GitHub notebooks are free.

title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd edition)
author_source: Rob J. Hyndman, George Athanasopoulos, 2021, OTexts, open textbook (R; a Python edition is in progress at https://otexts.com/fpppy/ (unverified, site blocked here))
note: Free, rigorous and readable; the standard text for the forecasting half of the course (decomposition, ETS, ARIMA, regression with ARIMA errors, hierarchical and grouped forecasting across countries and products).
course_use: Session 4 reading (chapters on time series regression, ARIMA and hierarchical forecasting). Free.

title: Bayesian Modeling and Computation in Python
author_source: Osvaldo A. Martin, Ravin Kumar, Junpeng Lao, 2021, Chapman and Hall/CRC, textbook, free online
note: Written by PyMC and ArviZ core developers; covers priors, MCMC diagnostics, hierarchical models and time series in exactly the stack PyMC-Marketing uses. The practical companion for anyone fitting a Bayesian MMM.
course_use: Session 2 background (chapters on Bayesian inference, hierarchical models, model comparison). Free online; print edition paywalled.

title: The Effect: An Introduction to Research Design and Causality
author_source: Nick Huntington-Klein, 2022, Chapman and Hall/CRC, textbook, free online with R, Stata and Python code
note: The friendliest serious causal-inference text; the chapters on difference-in-differences, synthetic control and event studies are exactly the toolkit behind geo experiments, GeoLift and CausalImpact.
course_use: Session 4 reading (difference-in-differences, synthetic control chapters) before the experiment lab. Free.

title: Causal Inference for the Brave and True
author_source: Matheus Facure, 2022 onward, open online book in Python (the author's O'Reilly book Causal Inference in Python, 2023, is the paid version (unverified))
note: Python-first, notebook-based treatment of potential outcomes, regression, DiD, synthetic control and uplift, written by a practitioner; students can run every chapter.
course_use: Session 4 lab companion (synthetic control and DiD chapters). Free.

title: Causal Inference: The Mixtape
author_source: Scott Cunningham, 2021, Yale University Press, textbook, free online with R, Stata and Python code
note: Clear, example-driven treatment of DAGs, matching, DiD and synthetic control; the DAG chapter is the best short preparation for Meridian's causal-graph framing of MMM.
course_use: Background for session 4; assign the DAG and synthetic control chapters. Free online.

title: Effective Advertising: Understanding When, How, and Why Advertising Works
author_source: Gerard J. Tellis, 2004, Sage, book
note: Synthesises decades of econometric and experimental evidence on advertising response: elasticities, carryover, wear-in and wear-out, and the comparison of field experiments with econometric estimates. The qualitative counterpart to the elasticity meta-analyses.
course_use: Session 1 background (chapters on advertising carryover and market-level effects). Paywalled; a scanned copy is on the Internet Archive lending library.

title: Empirical Generalizations about Marketing Impact (2nd edition)
author_source: Dominique M. Hanssens (ed.), 2015, Marketing Science Institute (Relevant Knowledge Series), book
note: About 120 one-page empirical generalisations (advertising elasticity, price elasticity, carryover, long-term effects, cross-country patterns), each with references. Ideal for setting Bayesian priors and for sanity-checking student MMM output.
course_use: Session 2 (prior elicitation exercise) and session 3. Paid MSI publication (about USD 40 as e-book); short extracts are quotable.

title: Principles of Marketing Engineering and Analytics (3rd edition)
author_source: Gary L. Lilien, Arvind Rangaswamy, Arnaud De Bruyn, 2017, DecisionPro, textbook with Excel tools (unverified)
note: The classic "marketing engineering" treatment of response functions and resource allocation (ADBUDG-style curves, allocation across segments and regions) with managerial cases; useful to show the pre-Bayesian logic of budget optimisation.
course_use: Background for session 3. Paywalled, with a student software licence.

title: Marketing Mix Modeling Best Practices (Nielsen with Google and Meta)
author_source: Nielsen, Google and Meta, 2022, report (PDF, about 20 pages)
note: The most-cited vendor-neutral checklist for model specification: model at the most granular geography available, include non-marketing drivers (a media-only MMM overstated ad ROI by 68 per cent in Nielsen's comparison), handle digital granularity and reach. Companion Nielsen note analyses 19 Japanese models to show regional beats national data.
course_use: Session 2 (data and model specification) required reading; pairs with the geo-hierarchy lab. Free.

title: Modernizing MMM: Best Practices for Marketers (IAB)
author_source: IAB (US) with MMM vendors, December 2025, report (PDF)
note: Newest vendor-neutral industry guide; frames "timely, auditable, decision-ready" MMM, covers calibration with experiments, cadence, governance and includes cross-industry case studies.
course_use: Session 1 (measurement landscape) and Session 5 (from model to decision); free.

title: Modern Measurement Playbook (Google)
author_source: Google / Think with Google, 2023 (updated 2024), report (PDF, 44 pages)
note: Sets out the "measurement tripod" (attribution, incrementality experiments, MMM) and how to triangulate them; concise and well illustrated, so it works as a framing text for the whole course.
course_use: Session 1 pre-reading; Session 5 for the triangulation discussion. Free.

title: The MMM Handbook: A Guide for Developing Impactful Marketing Mix Models (Google)
author_source: Google (Think with Google, EMEA), 2023, report (PDF, "a CMO's handbook")
note: Short management-level guide: start with the right business questions, pick KPIs, capture all drivers, validate, act. Good contrast to the technical Nielsen document.
course_use: Session 1 or background; free.

title: Meridian Playbook (Google)
author_source: Google, 2025, report (PDF)
note: Step-by-step guidance on running Google's open-source Bayesian MMM (data requirements, geo-level set-up, priors from experiments, budget optimiser). Directly transferable to a Python lab.
course_use: Session 3 (Bayesian MMM lab) or Session 4 (budget allocation); free.

title: ROI Genome (Analytic Partners)
author_source: Analytic Partners, ongoing series 2020 to 2025, reports and briefs
note: Meta-analysis across 1,000+ brands and 50 countries of MMM results: brand versus performance messaging, recession spend, CTV, scenario planning (25 to 70 per cent ROI gains). Rare cross-country benchmark material.
course_use: Session 4 (cross-country budget allocation) as discussion input; Session 5. Free summaries, full reports gated behind registration.

title: Marketing Mix Modelling: A How-To Guide for Marketers (WARC and Magic Numbers)
author_source: Dr Grace Kite (Magic Numbers) with WARC, 2023, report (PDF, five chapters)
note: Practical and candid on choosing suppliers, embedding MMM in an organisation, reading results and common failure modes; includes UK case studies. Written by an econometrician who runs models for a living.
course_use: Session 5 (using MMM in management) reading; free mirror, WARC version paywalled.

title: Profit Ability 2: The New Business Case for Advertising (Ebiquity and Thinkbox)
author_source: Ebiquity for Thinkbox with Gain Theory, EssenceMediacom, Mindshare and Wavemaker, May 2024, report (PDF)
note: Pooled MMM across GBP 1.8bn of UK media, 141 brands and 10 channels; shows short-term versus sustained profit ROI by channel (TV 5.61, online video 3.86, generic PPC 3.52) and that about 60 per cent of effect lands after 13 weeks. A clean example of what adstock and long-term effects mean commercially.
course_use: Session 2 (adstock and carry-over) and Session 4; free.

title: Paid Media Effectiveness Handbook (WFA and Ebiquity)
author_source: World Federation of Advertisers with Ebiquity, 2026, report
note: Based on research with advertisers controlling about USD 40bn of paid media; explains how MMM, attribution, experiments and brand metrics fit together and reports that 80 per cent use MMM but only 13 per cent turn data into insight quickly. The EMEA vendor benchmark is useful for a European vendor-selection discussion.
course_use: Session 5 and background; WFA members only (summary articles free).

title: Magic Quadrant for Marketing Mix Modeling Solutions (Gartner)
author_source: Gartner, November 2024 (first edition) and 2025 edition, analyst report; preceded by the Market Guide for MMM Solutions (April 2024)
note: The reference map of the commercial MMM vendor landscape (Leaders: Analytic Partners, Ipsos MMA, Ekimetrics, Nielsen and others) with Gartner's 2024 survey finding that 64 per cent of senior marketing leaders have adopted MMM. Useful to show students what "commercial tool" means versus open source.
course_use: Session 1 or 5, short discussion; paywalled, use vendor reprints.

title: The Forrester Wave: Marketing Measurement and Optimization
author_source: Forrester, Q3 2023 (solutions) and Q1 2026 (services), analyst reports
note: Nine providers scored on 38 criteria including global capabilities, unified measurement and model operations; complements Gartner.
course_use: Background for vendor comparison; reprints free, original paywalled.

title: Six Steps to More Effective Marketing Measurement (BCG)
author_source: Boston Consulting Group, 2025, article/report
note: Consultancy view with survey data: 39 per cent of leading marketers run MMM monthly, 40 per cent calibrate with incrementality tests, growing use of brand metrics in MMM. Good for the "MMM as a management system" angle.
course_use: Session 5 reading; free.

title: MMM adoption study (Kantar and Meta)
author_source: Kantar with Meta, 2025, report (PDF)
note: Global survey of 1,935 measurement professionals at companies spending over USD 1m a year on digital; adoption dynamics, barriers and what "good" looks like. Kantar's own MMM pages add the long-term brand-effect angle.
course_use: Session 1 background; free.

title: Market Mix Modelling Landscape Report 2025 (IAB Australia)
author_source: IAB Australia Ad Effectiveness Council, September 2025 (updated December 2025), report
note: Directory of twelve MMM vendors (classical econometrics to Bayesian and ML), a marketer's checklist and plain-language method comparison; a handy template for a vendor-evaluation exercise.
course_use: Session 5 exercise (evaluate a vendor pitch); free.

title: The Essential Guide to Marketing Mix Modeling and Multi-Touch Attribution (IAB and MMA Global)
author_source: IAB with MMA Global, November 2019, guidebook (PDF)
note: Older but still the clearest side-by-side of MMM and MTA (data, granularity, use cases, limitations). Meta's own note "Considerations for creating modern marketing mix models" (https://www.facebook.com/business/news/insights/considerations-for-creating-modern-marketing-mix-models) is a short complement.
course_use: Session 5 (attribution versus MMM); free.

title: Aggregate Advertising Models: The State of the Art
author_source: John D. C. Little, 1979, Operations Research 27(4), 629 to 667, article
note: The founding statement of what an advertising response model must capture: carryover, diminishing returns, competition, interaction and dynamics. Every adstock-plus-Hill MMM is a descendant.
course_use: Session 1 required reading (sections 1 to 4). Paywalled (INFORMS).

title: Econometric Measurement of the Duration of Advertising Effect on Sales
author_source: Darral G. Clarke, 1976, Journal of Marketing Research 13(4), 345 to 357, article
note: Shows that implied carryover depends heavily on the data interval (the data-interval bias), which is still the main reason weekly MMMs and annual studies disagree on decay rates.
course_use: Session 1 or 2 reading when introducing adstock decay. Paywalled (Sage/JSTOR).

title: The Persistence of Marketing Effects on Sales
author_source: Marnik G. Dekimpe, Dominique M. Hanssens, 1995, Marketing Science 14(1), 1 to 21, article
note: Introduces persistence modelling (unit roots, VAR, impulse responses) to separate short-run from long-run marketing effects; the methodological root of "long-term effects" claims in MMM.
course_use: Session 1 background; session 4 for time-series thinking. Paywalled.

title: How Well Does Advertising Work? Generalizations from Meta-Analysis of Brand Advertising Elasticities
author_source: Raj Sethuraman, Gerard J. Tellis, Richard A. Briesch, 2011, Journal of Marketing Research 48(3), 457 to 471, article
note: Mean short-term advertising elasticity 0.12, long-term 0.24, with moderators (durables, life-cycle stage, data interval, GRPs versus money, Europe versus US). The best single source of priors for a Bayesian MMM.
course_use: Session 2 required reading (use the moderator table to set priors). Paywalled, open PDF available.

title: A Meta-Analysis of Marketing Communication Carryover Effects
author_source: Christine Köhler, Murali K. Mantrala, Sönke Albers, Vamsi K. Kanuri, 2017, Journal of Marketing Research 54(6), article
note: Meta-analysis of carryover (decay) estimates across media and countries; gives defensible ranges for adstock parameters and shows how data interval and model type bias them.
course_use: Session 2 (adstock priors); pairs with Clarke 1976. Paywalled.

title: Demonstrating the Value of Marketing
author_source: Dominique M. Hanssens, Koen H. Pauwels, 2016, Journal of Marketing 80(6), 173 to 190, article
note: Frames marketing accountability as a chain from spend to metrics to financial value and reviews what response models, attribution and experiments can and cannot show. A good opening reading for managers-in-training.
course_use: Session 1 reading. Paywalled, open PDF available.

title: How T.V. Advertising Works: A Meta-Analysis of 389 Real World Split Cable T.V. Advertising Experiments
author_source: Leonard M. Lodish, Magid Abraham, Stuart Kalmenson, Jeanne Livelsberger, Beth Lubetkin, Bruce Richardson, Mary Ellen Stevens, 1995, Journal of Marketing Research 32(2), 125 to 139, article
note: The classic experimental benchmark: about half of TV weight tests show no significant sales effect, and effects are larger for new products. Sets expectations before students see MMM ROI claims.
course_use: Session 4 background (experiments versus models). Paywalled.

title: Bayesian Methods for Media Mix Modeling with Carryover and Shape Effects
author_source: Yuxue Jin, Yueqing Wang, Yunting Sun, David Chan, Jim Koehler, 2017, Google research white paper
note: The canonical modern MMM specification: geometric or delayed adstock plus a Hill saturation curve, estimated with Bayesian methods, with ROAS and marginal ROAS derived from the posterior. LightweightMMM, PyMC-Marketing and Meridian all implement it.
course_use: Session 2 required reading; reproduce its simulated example in the PyMC-Marketing lab. Free.

title: Geo-level Bayesian Hierarchical Media Mix Modeling
author_source: Yunting Sun, Yueqing Wang, Yuxue Jin, David Chan, Jim Koehler, 2017, Google research white paper
note: Pooling sub-national (geo) data in a hierarchical model gives tighter credible intervals than national data alone. This is the statistical justification for the country-by-region hierarchies in Meridian and for multi-country MMM.
course_use: Session 3 required reading (geo hierarchies across countries). Free.

title: Challenges and Opportunities in Media Mix Modeling
author_source: David Chan, Michael Perry, 2017, Google research white paper
note: Short, honest list of why MMM is hard: limited variation, collinearity, selection bias (ads follow demand), funnel effects, paid search, and the need for experiments. Excellent framing paper.
course_use: Session 1 or 2 reading; discussion piece. Free.

title: A Hierarchical Bayesian Approach to Improve Media Mix Models Using Category Data
author_source: Yueqing Wang, Yuxue Jin, Yunting Sun, David Chan, Jim Koehler, 2017, Google research white paper
note: Uses category-level data across brands as a hierarchical prior to stabilise a single brand's MMM; a practical answer to short series, and the same logic applies to pooling across countries.
course_use: Session 3 background. Free.

title: Introduction to the Aggregate Marketing System Simulator
author_source: Stephanie Zhang, Jon Vaver, 2017, Google research white paper; R package https://github.com/google/amss (verified, archived 2022)
note: A simulator that generates realistic aggregate marketing data with known ground-truth ROAS, so MMM methods can be tested. Ideal for teaching: students fit models to data where the true answer is known.
course_use: Session 2 or 4 lab (simulate, fit, compare to truth). Free, R.

title: Bayesian Hierarchical Media Mix Model Incorporating Reach and Frequency Data
author_source: Yingxiang Zhang, Mike Wurm, Alexander Wakim, Eddie Li, Ying Liu, 2023, Google research white paper
note: Extends the geo-hierarchical MMM to use reach and frequency instead of impressions, enabling optimal-frequency recommendations; this is the model inside Google Meridian (https://github.com/google/meridian, Apache-2.0, Python, verified).
course_use: Session 2 or 3 reading for the Meridian lab. Free.

title: Packaging Up Media Mix Modeling: An Introduction to Robyn's Open-Source Approach
author_source: Julian Runge, Igor Skokan, Gufeng Zhou, Koen Pauwels, 2024, arXiv 2403.14674 (Meta Marketing Science and academia), working paper
note: The authoritative description of Robyn: ridge regression, evolutionary hyperparameter search, Prophet decomposition, calibration with experiments and budget allocation, and the organisational reasons for the design. Good contrast to the Bayesian school.
course_use: Session 2 reading (compare with Jin et al. 2017). Free.

title: PyMC-Marketing: Bayesian marketing analytics in Python (JOSS)
author_source: PyMC Labs team, 2026 (year inferred from DOI series, unverified), Journal of Open Source Software, software paper
note: The citable reference for the Python library the course will most likely use: adstock and saturation transforms, lift-test calibration, time-varying effects, multidimensional (geo) models and budget optimisation.
course_use: Session 2 lab citation. Free, open access.

title: Bayesian Time Varying Coefficient Model with Applications to Marketing Mix Modeling
author_source: Edwin Ng, Zhishi Wang, Athena Dai (Uber), 2021, arXiv 2106.03322, working paper
note: Lets channel effectiveness drift over time via kernel-weighted regression, which matters for multi-year series and for markets in transition; also the basis of Uber's Orbit library.
course_use: Session 4 background (time-varying effects). Free.

title: Hierarchical Marketing Mix Models with Sign Constraints
author_source: Hao Chen, Minguang Zhang, Lanshan Han, Alvin Lim (Google), 2021, Journal of Applied Statistics (DOI 10.1080/02664763.2021.1946020 unverified); preprint arXiv 2008.12802
note: Multi-region hierarchical MMM with sign constraints on media coefficients, estimated with a scalable algorithm; directly relevant to multi-country models where naive regression gives negative media effects.
course_use: Session 3 background. Free preprint.

title: Your MMM is Broken: Identification of Nonlinear and Time-varying Effects in Marketing Mix Models
author_source: Ryan Dew, Nicolas Padilla, Anya Shchetkina (authors from memory, unverified), 2024, arXiv 2408.07678, working paper
note: Academic critique showing that standard MMMs cannot separately identify nonlinearity (saturation) from time variation without extra structure; a useful counterweight to vendor enthusiasm.
course_use: Session 2 or 4 discussion reading for stronger students. Free.

title: A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement: Evidence from Big Field Experiments at Facebook
author_source: Brett R. Gordon, Florian Zettelmeyer, Neha Bhargava, Dan Chapsky, 2019, Marketing Science 38(2), 193 to 225, article
note: Fifteen large Facebook experiments show that observational methods (matching, regression, last click) often miss true lift by a wide margin. The paper students should read before trusting any attribution or uncalibrated model.
course_use: Session 4 required reading. Paywalled, open PDF available.

title: Close Enough? A Large-Scale Exploration of Non-Experimental Approaches to Advertising Measurement
author_source: Brett R. Gordon, Robert Moakler, Florian Zettelmeyer, 2023, Marketing Science 42(4), 768 to 793, article
note: Follow-up on 663 experiments: even with rich data, non-experimental estimates are frequently far off, which motivates calibrating MMM with lift tests.
course_use: Session 4 reading (pairs with Gordon et al. 2019). Paywalled.

title: TV Advertising Effectiveness and Profitability: Generalizable Results from 288 Brands
author_source: Bradley T. Shapiro, Günter J. Hitsch, Anna E. Tuchman, 2021, Econometrica 89(4), 1855 to 1879, article
note: Panel-based causal estimates of TV elasticities for 288 brands; median elasticity is small and marginal ROI is negative for most brands. A sobering benchmark for MMM ROI outputs and budget recommendations.
course_use: Session 3 reading (budget allocation reality check). Paywalled, open PDF available.

title: Measuring Ad Effectiveness Using Geo Experiments
author_source: Jon Vaver, Jim Koehler, 2011, Google research white paper
note: The original geo-experiment design and geo-based regression (GBR) analysis; the template for every geo-lift test now used to calibrate MMMs.
course_use: Session 4 required reading before the geo-experiment lab. Free.

title: Estimating Ad Effectiveness Using Geo Experiments in a Time-Based Regression Framework
author_source: Jouni Kerman, Peng Wang, Jon Vaver, 2017, Google research white paper
note: Time-based regression (TBR) for geo tests with few regions, estimating the cumulative causal effect from a counterfactual time series; the method behind many European geo tests where countries have few media regions.
course_use: Session 4 reading. Free.

title: Robust Causal Inference for Incremental Return on Ad Spend with Randomized Paired Geo Experiments
author_source: Aiyou Chen, Timothy C. Au, 2022, Annals of Applied Statistics 16(1), article; preprint arXiv 1908.02922; Python package https://github.com/google/trimmed_match (verified)
note: Trimmed Match estimator for paired geo experiments that is robust to outlier regions; with the companion design paper (Chen, Longfils, Remy 2021, arXiv 2105.07060, verified) it gives a complete, open workflow for iROAS experiments.
course_use: Session 4 lab (trimmed_match on synthetic data). Free preprint; journal version paywalled.

title: Inferring Causal Impact Using Bayesian Structural Time-Series Models
author_source: Kay H. Brodersen, Fabian Gallusser, Jim Koehler, Nicolas Remy, Steven L. Scott, 2015, Annals of Applied Statistics 9(1), 247 to 274, article; package https://github.com/google/CausalImpact (verified)
note: The CausalImpact method: a Bayesian structural time-series counterfactual for a single treated market, widely used to read campaign launches and quasi-experiments in single countries.
course_use: Session 4 lab (tfcausalimpact in Python). Open access.

title: The Unfavorable Economics of Measuring the Returns to Advertising
author_source: Randall A. Lewis, Justin M. Rao, 2015, Quarterly Journal of Economics 130(4), 1941 to 1973, article
note: Shows why even huge experiments are underpowered for advertising ROI: sales variance dwarfs plausible ad effects. Essential for teaching power analysis of geo tests and the limits of calibration.
course_use: Session 4 reading. Paywalled; working-paper versions circulate.

title: Attributing Conversions in a Multichannel Online Marketing Environment: An Empirical Model and a Field Experiment
author_source: Hongshuang (Alice) Li, P. K. Kannan, 2014, Journal of Marketing Research 51(1), 40 to 56, article
note: The reference academic multi-touch attribution model (consideration, visit, purchase stages with carryover and spillover), validated with a field experiment; shows how last-click misallocates credit.
course_use: Session 5 required reading. Paywalled.

title: Beyond the Last Touch: Attribution in Online Advertising
author_source: Ron Berman, 2018, Marketing Science 37(5), 771 to 792, article
note: Game-theoretic analysis of attribution rules showing how last-touch distorts publisher incentives and why Shapley-type rules behave better; the theory behind data-driven attribution products.
course_use: Session 5 reading. Paywalled; SSRN version available.

title: The Path to Purchase and Attribution Modeling: Introduction to Special Section
author_source: P. K. Kannan, Werner Reinartz, Peter C. Verhoef, 2016, International Journal of Research in Marketing 33(3), 449 to 456, editorial article
note: Concise map of attribution research and of the gap between user-level attribution and aggregate MMM; the whole IJRM special section (de Haan, Wiesel, Pauwels; Anderl et al.; Kireyev, Pauwels, Gupta) is worth assigning.
course_use: Session 5 overview reading. Paywalled.

title: The Effectiveness of Different Forms of Online Advertising for Purchase Conversion in a Multiple-Channel Attribution Framework
author_source: Evert de Haan, Thorsten Wiesel, Koen Pauwels, 2016, International Journal of Research in Marketing 33(3), 491 to 507, article
note: Uses a VAR-based, aggregate time-series approach to attribute conversions across online channels, which is in effect an MMM applied to attribution; shows content-integrated ads and search outperform banners.
course_use: Session 5 reading (bridge between MMM and attribution). Paywalled.

title: Mapping the Customer Journey: Lessons Learned from Graph-Based Online Attribution Modeling
author_source: Eva Anderl, Ingo Becker, Florian von Wangenheim, Jan Hendrik Schumann, 2016, International Journal of Research in Marketing 33(3), 457 to 474, article
note: Markov-graph attribution (removal effects) on real clickstream data from German firms; the method behind many "data-driven attribution" tools, written by authors at ETH Zurich and Passau.
course_use: Session 5 lab (Markov attribution in Python). Paywalled.

title: Data-Driven Multi-Touch Attribution Models
author_source: Xuhui Shao, Lexin Li, 2011, Proceedings of KDD 2011, conference paper
note: The first widely cited algorithmic MTA (bagged logistic regression and a simple probabilistic model); short and easy to implement in a lab.
course_use: Session 5 lab reference. Paywalled (ACM), author copies circulate.

title: Integrated Marketing Attribution: A Bayesian Framework for Privacy-Safe Granular Measurement Anchored in MMM
author_source: authors not captured (unverified), 2026, arXiv 2606.16878, working paper
note: One of the first papers to formalise "unified measurement": granular attribution constrained to reconcile with an MMM's channel totals, in a privacy-safe setting after cookie loss. Timely for the MMM-versus-attribution debate.
course_use: Session 5 discussion reading. Free.

title: Dynamic Marketing Budget Allocation Across Countries, Products, and Marketing Activities
author_source: Marc Fischer, Sönke Albers, Nils Wagner, Monika Frie, 2011, Marketing Science 30(4), 568 to 585 (INFORMS Practice Prize winner), article
note: The Bayer case: a decision-support model that allocates marketing budgets across countries, products and activities using response elasticities and dynamics, with a claimed profit improvement of about EUR 500 million. The single best academic match for the course's international allocation theme.
course_use: Session 3 required reading and case discussion; rebuild the allocation heuristic in Python. Paywalled.

title: Marketing Mix and Brand Sales in Global Markets: Examining the Contingent Role of Country-Market Characteristics
author_source: S. Cem Bahadir, Sundar G. Bharadwaj, Rajendra K. Srivastava, 2015, Journal of International Business Studies 46(5), 596 to 619, article
note: Hierarchical linear model across 14 emerging and developed markets: advertising and product innovation matter more in emerging markets, distribution and price differ by country type. Gives students priors for how elasticities shift across countries.
course_use: Session 3 reading (international angle). Paywalled.

title: A Global Perspective on the Marketing Mix across Time and Space
author_source: Julian Wichmann, Abhinav Uppal, Amalesh Sharma, Marnik G. Dekimpe, 2022, International Journal of Research in Marketing 39(2), 502 to 521, article
note: Reviews cross-country marketing-mix effectiveness research and sets a research agenda on heterogeneity across markets and over time; the most recent academic overview of the international MMM question.
course_use: Session 3 background reading. Paywalled.

title: Determinants of Advertising Effectiveness: The Development of an International Advertising Elasticity Database and a Meta-Analysis
author_source: Sina Henningsen, Rebecca Heuke, Michel Clement, 2011, Business Research 4(2), 193 to 239, article (open access)
note: Meta-analysis of advertising elasticities built on an explicitly international database (mean current-period elasticity 0.09) with country and method moderators; complements Sethuraman et al. 2011 and is free.
course_use: Session 2 or 3 (priors by country). Open access.

title: The Role of National Culture in Advertising's Sensitivity to Business Cycles: An Investigation Across Continents
author_source: Barbara Deleersnyder, Marnik G. Dekimpe, Jan-Benedict E. M. Steenkamp, Peter S. H. Leeflang, 2009, Journal of Marketing Research 46(5), 623 to 636, article
note: 37 countries over 25 years: advertising is procyclical, and the degree depends on national culture (uncertainty avoidance, long-term orientation). Shows why macro controls and country effects belong in a multi-market MMM.
course_use: Session 3 background. Paywalled.

title: Price and Advertising Effectiveness over the Business Cycle
author_source: Harald J. van Heerde, Maarten J. Gijsenberg, Marnik G. Dekimpe, Jan-Benedict E. M. Steenkamp, 2013, Journal of Marketing Research 50(2), 177 to 193, article
note: Time-varying elasticities over 25 years show price sensitivity rises and advertising effectiveness falls in contractions; a concrete reason to model time-varying coefficients and macro conditions.
course_use: Session 4 reading (time-varying effects). Paywalled, open PDF available.

title: Financial Development and Country-Level Advertising Spending: The Moderating Role of Economic Development and National Culture
author_source: Berrak Bahadir, S. Cem Bahadir, 2020, Journal of International Marketing 28(4), article
note: Country-level panel on what drives advertising intensity across economies; useful context when students compare budgets and media prices across markets.
course_use: Session 3 background. Paywalled.

title: Optimizable and Implementable Aggregate Response Modeling for Marketing Decision Support
author_source: Sönke Albers, 2012, International Journal of Research in Marketing 29(2), 111 to 122, article
note: Argues that response models must be both optimisable (concave, interpretable elasticities) and implementable (simple enough for managers), and shows how to go from elasticities to allocation rules. The academic underpinning of the budget optimisers in Robyn and Meridian.
course_use: Session 3 required reading. Paywalled, SSRN copy available.

title: The Value of Empirical Generalizations in Marketing
author_source: Dominique M. Hanssens, 2018, Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science 46, 6 to 8, editorial
note: Three-page argument for using generalisations (elasticity ranges, carryover) as priors and sanity checks; a quick companion to the MSI book above.
course_use: Session 2 short reading. Paywalled; open PDF on the UCLA Anderson site (listed in search).

title: Marketing's Impact on Firm Value: Generalizations from a Meta-Analysis
author_source: Alexander Edeling, Marc Fischer, 2016, Journal of Marketing Research 53(4), 515 to 534, article
note: Meta-analysis linking advertising, brand and other marketing assets to firm value; provides the "so what" for MMM results at board level and a Cologne-based author who fits the DACH guest-speaker focus.
course_use: Session 1 or 3 background. Paywalled.

title: How Advertising Works: What Do We Really Know?
author_source: Demetrios Vakratsas, Tim Ambler, 1999, Journal of Marketing 63(1), 26 to 43, review article
note: Reviews 250 studies on advertising response and frameworks (hierarchy of effects, carryover, wear-out); the best short literature map before reading MMM papers.
course_use: Session 1 background. Paywalled.

title: Marvelous Advertising Returns? A Meta-Analysis of Advertising Elasticities in the Entertainment Industry
author_source: authors not captured (unverified), 2022, Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, article
note: Recent, industry-specific meta-analysis of advertising elasticities; a template for how students can derive sector priors for their own MMM.
course_use: Session 2 optional reading. Paywalled (check for Springer open access).

title: PyMC Labs blog
author_source: PyMC Labs (authors include Thomas Wiecki, Juan Orduz, Carlos Trujillo, Will Dean), 2021 to 2026, blog
note: The home of PyMC-Marketing thinking: Bayesian MMM, time-varying effectiveness, funnel-aware models, lift-test calibration, the HelloFresh case. Python code throughout.
course_use: Sessions 2 to 4 lab readings; free.

title: Google Meridian documentation and repository
author_source: Google, 2025 to 2026, website and software (Python, Apache 2.0)
note: Reference docs for a hierarchical geo-level Bayesian MMM with reach and frequency, experiment priors and budget optimiser; Colab tutorial with sample data; superseded LightweightMMM (https://github.com/google/lightweight_mmm, archived, fetched).
course_use: Session 3 and 4 labs; free.

title: Meta Robyn site and repository
author_source: Meta Marketing Science (Gufeng Zhou and others), 2021 to 2026, website and software (R primary, Python beta, MIT)
note: Ridge regression plus evolutionary hyperparameter search, calibration with lift tests, simulated weekly demo data; the most used open-source MMM in practice and the natural contrast to the Bayesian tools.
course_use: Session 3 comparison (R versus Python), optional lab; free.

title: Recast blog and MMM Academy
author_source: Recast (Michael Kaminsky, Thomas Vladeck), 2021 to 2026, blog and newsletter
note: The most opinionated practitioner writing on MMM identification problems, geo-test calibration, long-term brand effects and vendor hype; the "who is talking about MMM" page lists public brand examples.
course_use: Session 3 (calibration) and Session 5; free.

title: Dr Juan Camilo Orduz, personal blog
author_source: Juan Camilo Orduz (PyMC Labs, Berlin), 2021 to 2026, blog
note: Fully reproducible PyMC notebooks on adstock, saturation, time-varying coefficients, Orbit's KTR model and hierarchical MMM; ideal lab scaffolding. Berlin-based, so also a realistic guest-speaker lead for the people part.
course_use: Sessions 2 and 3 lab material; free.

title: Aryma Labs Substack
author_source: Venkat Raman and Ridhima Kumar (Aryma Labs, India), 2023 to 2026, newsletter
note: Critical, statistically careful posts ("is MMM just linear regression?", "one true MMM?", lessons from FMCG econometrics); good for teaching scepticism towards automated tools.
course_use: Session 2 discussion reading; free.

title: Measured learning centre
author_source: Measured (US), 2020 to 2026, website
note: Decision tree for when to use incrementality tests, attribution or MMM; a "how to QA an MMM" checklist; ten named brand examples. Vendor site but unusually instructive.
course_use: Session 5; free.

title: Haus blog and Incrementality School
author_source: Haus (US; founders from Netflix and Google experimentation teams), 2023 to 2026, blog
note: Clear explanations of geo experiments, synthetic control and "causal MMM" built on experiments; the experiments-first counterweight to model-first vendors.
course_use: Session 3 or the experiments session; free.

title: Sellforte blog
author_source: Sellforte (Helsinki), 2022 to 2026, blog
note: European SaaS vendor writing on retail and e-commerce MMM, causal MMM and a procurement/RFP guide that students can use in a vendor-selection exercise.
course_use: Session 5 exercise; free.

title: Mutinex (Henry Innis) and Madison and Wall interviews
author_source: Mutinex (Sydney) and Madison and Wall Substack (Brian Wieser), 2024 to 2026, blog and newsletter
note: The "always-on MMM feeding bidding systems" thesis and a sceptical industry analyst's questioning of it; good for a debate on MMM cadence and over-use of incrementality tests.
course_use: Session 5 debate; free.

title: Cassandra resources
author_source: Cassandra (European MMM SaaS), 2023 to 2026, website
note: Readable walk-through of the algorithm behind a commercial MMM and optimiser, written for marketers rather than statisticians.
course_use: Session 4 background; free.

title: Ebiquity Insights blog
author_source: Ebiquity (London), 2022 to 2026, blog
note: The classical econometrics view: "Bayesian MMM: cure-all or caveat emptor?", pros and cons of always-on automation, MMM as a management discipline; strong European advertiser perspective.
course_use: Session 3 counter-reading; free.

title: MASS Analytics blog and Measure Up podcast
author_source: MASS Analytics (Tunis and London), 2020 to 2026, blog and podcast
note: Structured "learn MMM" curriculum, masterclasses and an interview podcast with practitioners; the geo-experiment explainer is concise.
course_use: Background self-study; free.

title: Hands-On Data: "The hard thing about Marketing Mix Models"
author_source: Hands-On Data (independent data scientist), 2024, Substack post
note: Honest practitioner account of identification, data and organisational problems in MMM; short and quotable.
course_use: Session 2 warm-up; free.

title: Vexpower MMM learning path (Mike Taylor)
author_source: Mike Taylor (Vexpower, former Ladder agency), 2022 to 2025, simulator-based courses
note: Scenario-style exercises (Robyn, LightweightMMM, Orbit) that mimic client briefs; a model for how to write lab assignments.
course_use: Inspiration for assignments; paid subscription, some free content.

title: Thomas Wiecki, "Bayesian Marketing Science: Solving Marketing's 3 Biggest Problems" (PyCon DE and PyData Berlin 2023)
author_source: PyMC Labs, 2023, video (YouTube, about 30 minutes, free, intermediate).
note: Introduces PyMC-Marketing (MMM and CLV) and CausalPy in one talk with code, from the PyMC founder. A good conceptual opener before the lab.
course_use: S2 pre-class viewing.

title: PyMC Labs, "Bayesian Marketing Mix Models: State of the Art and their Future" (online meetup, September 2022)
author_source: PyMC Labs with Juan Orduz, Luca Fiaschi and guests, 2022, video (recording linked from PyMC Discourse; about 60 to 90 minutes, free, intermediate).
note: Practitioner panel on what works in Bayesian MMM at companies such as HelloFresh and Bolt; useful as a "voices from industry" segment.
course_use: Background.

title: PyData NYC 2024, "PyMC-Marketing: Customer and Marketing Analytics the Easy Way" (Christian Luhmann)
author_source: PyData, November 2024, talk (40 minutes; recording expected on the PyData YouTube channel, unverified).
note: Most recent conference walk-through of the library's MMM and CLV APIs.
course_use: S2 optional viewing.

title: Google Ads DevCast, episode 6: "The What and Why on Meridian" (May 2026)
author_source: Google Advertising and Measurement Developers, 2026, video podcast (YouTube playlist, about 30 minutes, free, introductory).
note: Official overview of Meridian and the new surfaces (Google Analytics, Studio, GeoX) from the product team; up to date as of 2026.
course_use: S3 pre-class viewing.

title: Meridian Python tutorials on YouTube
author_source: Third-party creators, 2025, videos: "Meridian Marketing Mix Modeling: Python Tutorial" and "Meridian Tutorial: Building a National MMM for eCommerce" (each roughly 20 to 40 minutes, free, intermediate; channels unverified).
note: Step-by-step runs of the official Meridian demo notebook, useful for students who get stuck installing TensorFlow Probability.
course_use: S3 lab support material. Google's own "Meridian Self-starter Guide for CMOs" PDF (Think with Google, search-confirmed) is a non-technical companion.

title: Recast, "How to Build a Media Mix Model (MMM)" series with Tom Vladeck
author_source: Recast, 2024 to 2025, YouTube playlist (multi-episode, 15 to 30 minutes each, free, intermediate; episode 2 covers DAGs in MMM) plus "How to Use Lift Tests to Calibrate Your MMM".
note: Statistician-led, vendor-neutral in tone, explicit about causal assumptions and validation; complements the code-centric talks.
course_use: S2 and S5 viewing.

title: MASS Analytics free MMM course on YouTube (Dr Ramla Jarrar)
author_source: MASS Analytics, 2023 to 2026, YouTube playlists (eleven "Packs" A to K following a real project order; dozens of short videos, free, beginner to intermediate).
note: The only free end-to-end MMM project curriculum (data splitting, transformations, modelling, optimisation, reporting) from a practising vendor; tool-agnostic in the concepts.
course_use: S1 to S3 self-study; assign specific packs.

title: MASS Analytics MMM Academy (Fundamentals and End-to-End courses)
author_source: MASS Analytics, 2025 to 2026, paid online courses (2 courses, 9 modules, real datasets, certificate, access to MassTer software; price not public, search-confirmed).
note: Covers Bayesian and hierarchical models and board-level reporting; one of the few MMM certificates. Worth asking about an academic bundle for 30 students.
course_use: Optional for ambitious students; vendor contact.

title: PyMC Labs, "Bayesian Marketing Analytics" live course
author_source: PyMC Labs, 2025 to 2026, live online course (four weeks, cohort based, paid; price and next dates not retrievable in this session).
note: Taught by the PyMC-Marketing authors; covers MMM, causal inference, CLV, product adoption and budget optimisation, so it mirrors this course almost module by module.
course_use: Instructor preparation; possible guest lecture by a PyMC Labs instructor.

title: Meta Robyn walkthroughs
author_source: Gufeng Zhou (Robyn creator) interview "Robyn's Creation to Controversy, Decomposition Distance and MMM Politics" (2024, about 60 minutes, free); "Ep. 1 to Ep. 8 Marketing Mix Modeling with Facebook Robyn" tutorial series (third party, 2022 to 2023, 10 to 25 minutes each, free, intermediate R).
note: The interview explains design choices (DECOMP.RSSD, ridge, Nevergrad) and their critics from the author himself; the episode series is the practical R walkthrough. Meta's own 15-minute demo video is hosted on Google Drive via the Robyn repo (unverified).
course_use: S2 optional viewing.

title: Posit, "Strategic Budget Optimization through Marketing Mix Modeling" (February 2026)
author_source: Posit Open Source (Isabella Velasquez and Daniel Chen), 2026, video (about 60 minutes, free, intermediate; R and Python).
note: Recent, tool-focused session on turning MMM output into a constrained budget plan.
course_use: S3 viewing.

title: Coursera, "Forecasting Models for Marketing Decisions" (Emory University)
author_source: Emory University on Coursera, 2023, MOOC (4 modules, roughly 10 to 15 hours, beginner to intermediate, free to audit, certificate paid; part of Foundations of Marketing Analytics specialisation).
note: Regression-based forecasting for marketing mix decisions in a business-school framing; closest MOOC match to S4.
course_use: S4 supplementary.

title: Coursera, "Data Analytics Methods for Marketing" (Meta)
author_source: Meta on Coursera, 2022, MOOC (about 20 hours, beginner, free to audit; module on marketing mix modelling and attribution).
note: Platform-side view of MMM, incrementality and attribution; useful for students without a stats background.
course_use: Background for weaker students.

title: LinkedIn Learning, "Marketing Attribution and Mix Modeling" (Michael Taylor) and "Introduction to Attribution and Mix Modeling" (Corey Koberg)
author_source: LinkedIn Learning, 2023 to 2024, video courses (1 h 38 min and 1 h 41 min, intermediate, subscription or free trial; certificates).
note: Taylor's course does a simple MMM with diminishing-returns transformations and scenario forecasting in a spreadsheet; Koberg's covers how MTA and MMM fit together. Short enough to assign fully.
course_use: S5 (attribution) pre-reading. WU may have LinkedIn Learning access via the library.

title: Udemy, "MMM Masterclass: Facebook Robyn Tutorial for Marketing" and "Fundamentals of Marketing Mix Modeling: Learn by Doing" (MASS Analytics)
author_source: Udemy, 2022 to 2025, video courses (typically 3 to 6 hours, intermediate; paid, often discounted to under EUR 20; MASS course includes a 2-week MassTer licence).
note: Cheapest structured hands-on routes into Robyn (R) and a GUI MMM tool respectively. A Japanese-language "Excel x Python MMM" course also exists for complete beginners.
course_use: Optional self-study.

title: DataCamp, "Building Response Models in R"
author_source: DataCamp, 2019, interactive course (4 hours, intermediate, subscription; DataCamp Classrooms gives free access to university instructors and their students).
note: Market response modelling with price and promotion effects, the closest DataCamp has to MMM; no Python MMM course exists there, though their "Decoding Marketing Mix Modeling" tutorial is a short free read.
course_use: S1 supplementary; apply for DataCamp Classrooms if the cohort wants R.

title: edX, "Fundamentals of Digital Marketing" (University of Maryland)
author_source: University of Maryland on edX, 2021 to 2024, MOOC (about 4 weeks, beginner, free to audit).
note: Only edX course found that explicitly covers attribution and MMM; conceptual, not quantitative.
course_use: Background only.

title: Industry conference content: Meta MMM Summit highlights and JSM 2025 Meridian session
author_source: Recast summary of Meta's Marketing Mix Modeling Summit (panels with Nielsen, Accenture, Ekimetrics), 2024; American Statistical Association JSM 2025 session "Meridian: Google's Open-Source MMM" (abstract only).
note: No dedicated "MMM conference" with public video archive exists; these two are the best proxies for what vendors and statisticians are debating (granularity, calibration, reach and frequency).
course_use: Background; discussion prompts.

title: Multiple Regression and Marketing-Mix Models (Darden technical note)
author_source: Rajkumar Venkatesan and Shea Gibbs, Darden Business Publishing, 2013, case/technical note; Darden UVA-M-0855, HBP UV6764, Case Centre 118828
note: The standard classroom note on regression-based MMM (omitted-variable bias, interpretation of coefficients, elasticities); used in Darden's Big Data in Marketing elective.
course_use: Session 2 pre-reading; paid (about USD 5 to 9 per student via HBP or Case Centre).

title: Note on Marketing Mix Models: Evaluating "Bang for the Buck" (Darden)
author_source: Paul W. Farris, Darden Business Publishing, 1987, technical note M-0339
note: The classic resource-allocation framing of MMM (marginal returns, response curves) that today's optimisers still implement; short and still assigned.
course_use: Session 4 background; paid, low cost.

title: Digital Marketing at HBS Online (HBS case 521-027)
author_source: Sunil Gupta and Rajiv Lal, Harvard Business School, 2020 (revised 2024), case; Case Centre 174588
note: Management must allocate a digital budget across channels and course portfolios using channel performance data; raises attribution versus incrementality and portfolio trade-offs with real numbers.
course_use: Session 4 or 5 case discussion; paid (HBP, about USD 9 per student plus teaching note).

title: Amperity: First-Party Data at a Crossroads (HBS case 524-017)
author_source: Elie Ofek, Hema Yoganarasimhan and Alexis Lefort, Harvard Business School, 2024, case
note: Sets the signal-loss and privacy context (cookie deprecation, first-party data) that explains why MMM is back; good opener before the technical sessions.
course_use: Session 1 case; paid (HBP).

title: Cutting-Edge Marketing Analytics: Real World Cases and Data Sets (Darden casebook)
author_source: Rajkumar Venkatesan, Paul Farris and Ronald Wilcox, FT Press, 2014, book of cases with datasets; successor "Marketing Analytics: Essential Tools for Data-Driven Decisions", UVA Press, 2021
note: Each chapter is a real company case with downloadable data (regression-based marketing-mix, resource allocation, experiments, CLV); the cases can be run in Python rather than the book's Excel/R.
course_use: Sessions 2 and 4 labs; book purchase or per-case licences.

title: Advertising measurement at Facebook and eBay (research-based mini-cases, Kellogg and Berkeley)
author_source: Brett Gordon, Florian Zettelmeyer, Neha Bhargava and Dan Chapsky, Marketing Science 2019 (SSRN 2017); Thomas Blake, Chris Nosko and Steven Tadelis, Econometrica 2015; Gordon, Moakler and Zettelmeyer, Marketing Science 2023, articles usable as cases
note: No formal Kellogg case on MMM was found, but these are the canonical "observational methods versus experiments" teaching materials: eBay paid-search returns were a fraction of non-experimental estimates; Facebook's 15 RCTs show how far attribution and matching stray from lift.
course_use: Session 5 (attribution versus incrementality) as a structured discussion; journal access via WU library, slides free.

title: Resident and Robyn (Meta Marketing Science case)
author_source: Meta, 2021, published case study (free)
note: E-commerce company (Nectar, DreamCloud) runs its in-house MMM alongside Robyn, uses DMA-level data and lift-test calibration, reports 20 per cent revenue growth; the same page lists Central Retail Group (Thailand) and Lemonade. A free case with a reproducible open-source tool.
course_use: Session 3 case plus Robyn demo data; free.

title: Marketing Mix Modeling in Lemonade (arXiv paper as case)
author_source: Lemonade data science team, 2025, working paper arXiv 2501.01276
note: Candid account of building a Bayesian MMM for an insurtech, combining it with Robyn and geo tests for calibration; reads like a teaching case with methods detail.
course_use: Session 3 reading; free.

title: Advertising incrementality using controlled geo-experiments: the Universal App Campaign case (Uber)
author_source: Joel Barajas and colleagues (Uber), AdKDD 2020, conference paper
note: A full geo-experiment case: market pairing, Bayesian structural time series counterfactual, a 6.57 per cent conversion drop when Google UAC spend is paused; reusable as a lab on geo tests that feed MMM priors.
course_use: Session 3 or experiments session lab; free.

title: Structural estimation of MMM parameters from geo-experiments (Zalando researcher)
author_source: Niklas Heusch (Zalando), 2026, working paper arXiv 2608.21128
note: Shows a standard MMM reporting 10.61x ROAS for paid search whose experimental truth was 4.20x, and how geo-experiment time series recover the right parameters; a Berlin e-commerce example students will recognise.
course_use: Session 3 case; free.

title: Free datasets usable as cases
author_source: various, 2020 to 2026, open data
note: The multidimensional PyMC-Marketing example and Meridian's simulated data are geo-level, so they support a cross-country or cross-region assignment; the credibility files let students calibrate against lift tests.
course_use: Sessions 2 to 4 labs and the group project; all free.

title: HelloFresh: Bayesian MMM across 15 markets (PyMC Labs)
author_source: PyMC Labs, 2022 to 2025, case study and blog posts
note: Berlin-based meal-kit company replaces black-box attribution with a Bayesian MMM over TV, social, podcasts and partners; reported 60 per cent lower prediction variance, 10x faster inference and about 30 per cent ROAS uplift across 15 markets, with a what-if budget simulator. The best multi-country Python example available.
course_use: Session 4 anchor example and guest-talk target; free.

title: Heineken: MMM lighthouse markets Spain and Brazil (Meta)
author_source: Meta Business, 2021 to 2023, case study; AudienceProject cross-media case 2023
note: Global brewer uses two lighthouse markets to test measurement questions before rolling out; MMM showed Facebook ROI 2.3x the total media ROI in Spain and 3.5x the average in Brazil, now used as a "compass" for ongoing media decisions. Platform-sponsored, so discuss source bias.
course_use: Session 4 cross-country example; free.

title: Zalando: experiments first, then MMM (engineering blog and research)
author_source: Zalando Engineering, 2019, blog; Niklas Heusch, 2026, arXiv paper
note: Europe's largest fashion platform runs geo-based and audience-based randomised tests across 25 markets to measure incremental revenue, profit and acquisition, and its researchers now publish on reconciling MMM with those tests.
course_use: Session 3 and 5; free.

title: Uber: Orbit, in-house Bayesian MMM and geo experiments
author_source: Uber Marketing Data Science (Edwin Ng, Zhishi Wang, Athena Dai), 2021, paper and open-source library; Barajas et al., AdKDD 2020
note: Time-varying-coefficient Bayesian MMM built from zero in-house, with lift tests ingested as priors; documents how a global platform company operationalises measurement.
course_use: Session 3 (time-varying effects) example; free.

title: Bayer: unifying MMM and multi-touch attribution (TransUnion)
author_source: TransUnion, 2023, vendor case study
note: Leverkusen-based pharma and consumer-health group had conflicting MMM and MTA numbers; case describes aligning the two into one measurement programme. Short but a real DACH-headquartered example of the "unified measurement" problem.
course_use: Session 5 discussion; free.

title: Resident, Central Retail Group and Lemonade (Meta Robyn adopters)
author_source: Meta Marketing Science, 2021 to 2024, case studies
note: Three documented open-source MMM deployments: a US DTC group (+20 per cent revenue), a Thai retail conglomerate (budget reallocation worth up to 28 per cent revenue) and an insurtech using geo tests for calibration. Shows what adoption looks like outside the big consultancies.
course_use: Session 3; free.

title: Kellogg's: faster MMM turnaround (MASS Analytics)
author_source: MASS Analytics, 2022, vendor case study
note: FMCG example that treats media and trade spend together and focuses on speed of model refresh, which is the practical bottleneck in most MMM programmes.
course_use: Session 5; free.

title: Akulaku, Suntory Wellness and Finder: Meridian in APAC (Think with Google)
author_source: Google / Think with Google APAC, 2025, case articles
note: Early Meridian deployments in Indonesia, Japan and Australia; Akulaku's optimiser suggested 16 per cent more GMV at constant budget. Emerging-market angle, with the usual caveat that the platform publishes the results.
course_use: Session 4 international examples; free.

title: Nielsen and TikTok MMM case study
author_source: Nielsen, 2022, case study (PDF)
note: Shows how a new channel gets measured inside a commercial MMM and how platform data partnerships shape results.
course_use: Session 2 (channel data) example; free.

title: Caritas Switzerland and Swiss Post: cross-media MMM for a fundraising campaign (Exactag)
author_source: Swiss Post Advertising / Exactag, 2023, case summary in German
note: A DACH example: MMM on the "Welt ohne Armut" Christmas campaign attributed over half of donations to advertising, with direct mail most effective, then OOH and DOOH. Useful for students who read German and for the non-profit angle.
course_use: Session 2 or 4 short example; free.

title: Measured: ten named brand MMM examples
author_source: Measured, 2025, vendor article
note: Ten retail and DTC brands with one-paragraph outcomes from incrementality-calibrated MMM; a quick source of discussion vignettes. Search results also state that Unilever uses Measured for media measurement at scale (unverified detail).
course_use: Session 5 warm-up; free.

title: Volkswagen: cross-media measurement across Germany, France and the UK (TikTok and Kantar)
author_source: TikTok for Business with Kantar, 2023, case study
note: Not an MMM, but a three-country cross-media study for the ID. range that shows how brand-lift and reach studies feed into mix decisions; no public VW MMM was found.
course_use: Session 4 side example; free.

title: Anonymised vendor cases from Gain Theory and Ipsos MMA
author_source: Gain Theory (WPP), 2023, case study; Ipsos MMA, 2024, case study
note: A multinational alcoholic-beverages company and a large financial-services firm; useful to show how consultancies present MMM programmes (governance, scenario planning), even if client names are withheld.
course_use: Session 5 background; free.

title: Austrian and German market context
author_source: Trending Topics (Vienna), 2025, article; ad agents and directpoint articles, 2024 to 2025
note: German-language coverage of MMM adoption in DACH (one source cites about a quarter of companies using MMM regularly; unverified figure). No public, named MMM implementation from an Austrian brand (Red Bull, Swarovski, Spar, A1) was found.
course_use: Background; free.

title: PyMC-Marketing
author_source: PyMC Labs, 2023 to 2026, software (Python, Apache 2.0). Latest release 1.2.0, 29 September 2026; requires Python 3.12 or newer.
note: The most complete open Bayesian MMM in Python: pluggable adstock and saturation, lift-test calibration, time-varying intercept and media effects via Hilbert-space Gaussian processes, budget optimiser with constraints, multidimensional (geo-level) MMM, plus CLV models. Mature, actively released, excellent example notebooks.
course_use: S2 and S3 main lab tool; S5 calibration lab. Free.

title: Google Meridian
author_source: Google, 2025 to 2026, software (Python on TensorFlow Probability, Apache 2.0). Latest release 2.1.0, 25 September 2026; Python 3.10 or newer (repo states 3.11 to 3.13).
note: Geo-level hierarchical Bayesian MMM with Hill saturation, adstock, ROI priors, reach and frequency, and a fixed or flexible budget optimiser with ROI constraints. The natural "international" tool: geos (countries, regions) are first-class and partially pooled. Replaces LightweightMMM.
course_use: S3 lab (multi-country allocation) and comparison with PyMC-Marketing. Free; GPU helpful but not required for the demo data.

title: Orbit (KTR) by Uber
author_source: Uber, 2020 to 2026, software (Python, Apache 2.0). Latest 1.1.5.1, 22 May 2026; Python 3.12 or newer.
note: Bayesian time-series package whose Kernel Time-varying Regression (KTR) model is the reference implementation of the Ng, Wang and Dai (2021) time-varying coefficient MMM. Also provides ETS, LGT and DLT forecasters.
course_use: S4 (forecasting) and an advanced S2 demo of time-varying media effects. Free.

title: CausalPy
author_source: PyMC Labs, 2022 to 2026, software (Python, Apache 2.0). Latest 0.9.0, 28 July 2026.
note: One API for difference-in-differences (including staggered), synthetic control, geographical lift, interrupted time series, regression discontinuity, IV and IPW, with PyMC (Bayesian) or scikit-learn (OLS) back ends. Ideal for teaching quasi-experiments without R.
course_use: S5 lab (DiD, synthetic control on a country roll-out). Free.

title: GeoLift
author_source: Meta (facebookincubator), 2021 to 2026, software (R, GPL 2 or later; version 2.7.5 in DESCRIPTION).
note: End-to-end geo-experiment toolkit built on augmented synthetic control: power analysis and market selection, test design, lift inference and plots. Needs 25 or more pre-periods and about 20 or more geo units, which is a useful teaching constraint. R only.
course_use: S5 reading and optional R demo; pair with CausalPy or Google's Trimmed Match (https://github.com/google/trimmed_match, Python, Apache 2.0) for a Python path.

title: CausalImpact (tfcausalimpact Python port)
author_source: Willian Fuks (port of Google's R CausalImpact, Brodersen et al. 2015), 2020 to 2026, software (Python, Apache 2.0). Latest 0.0.19, 20 September 2026.
note: Bayesian structural time-series counterfactual for a single treated series with control series, with results documented as equivalent to the R original. Good for "what did the campaign or price change do" questions where no geo split exists.
course_use: S5 short lab. Free.

title: statsmodels
author_source: statsmodels developers, 2009 to 2026, software (Python, BSD 3-clause). Latest 0.15.0, 27 August 2026.
note: OLS and log-log elasticities with proper inference tables, HAC standard errors, VIF and condition numbers for multicollinearity diagnostics, ETS and SARIMAX for forecasting. The baseline every MMM should be compared against.
course_use: S1 lab (first MMM as OLS), S4 forecasting baselines. Free.

title: linearmodels
author_source: Kevin Sheppard, 2017 to 2025, software (Python, NCSA licence). Latest 7.0, 21 October 2025.
note: Panel estimators that statsmodels lacks: one- and two-way fixed effects, first differences, between and pooled, plus IV and system estimators, with clustered standard errors. The frequentist counterpart to partial pooling for country-by-week panels.
course_use: S3 lab (country fixed effects versus hierarchical priors). Free.

title: Prophet and StatsForecast (forecasting baselines)
author_source: Meta (Prophet 1.5.0, 5 October 2026, MIT) and Nixtla (StatsForecast 2.1.1, 16 July 2026, Apache 2.0), software (Python).
note: Prophet gives an additive trend plus Fourier seasonality plus holidays model with regressors, which doubles as an intuition builder for MMM baselines. StatsForecast gives fast AutoARIMA, AutoETS, Theta and CES with exogenous regressors across hundreds of country series at once.
course_use: S4 lab (country-level demand forecasts feeding budget scenarios). Free.

title: Synthetic MMM benchmark generators
author_source: Niklas Heusch, 2026, software and paper (Jupyter, generator for "A Synthetic Benchmark Dataset with Endogenous Marketing Spend for Validating MMMs", arXiv 2608.21130); Meta siMMMulator (R, MIT); PyMC Labs mmm-param-recovery (Python, Apache 2.0, compares PyMC samplers and Meridian).
note: Ground-truth data is the only way to grade an MMM. Heusch's generator is the first with endogenous spend (budget feedback, promo-calendar anticipation, TV bursts, performance chasing) plus simulated go-dark geo tests, which is exactly the confounding students need to see. No licence file shown on the Heusch repo.
course_use: S2 and S3 assignments (fit a model, compare to known ROI); S5 for simulated geo tests. Free.

title: Mutinex (GrowthOS)
author_source: Mutinex, Sydney, 2020 to 2026, software and vendor (continuous MMM, scenario planning, agency partnerships such as dentsu).
note: Example of "always-on" MMM delivered as a platform with confidence intervals on scenarios; strong APAC and multi-market footprint. No academic programme found.
course_use: Background; vendor-landscape slide in S3.

title: Cassandra
author_source: Cassandra (http://cassandra.app), 2021 to 2026, software and vendor (no-code Bayesian MMM and geo incrementality; now offers a Meridian-based model).
note: Shows how open-source engines (Meridian) are wrapped into SaaS. Markets a free entry tier ("Your MMM in 10 minutes"), which could give students a hands-on UI without code (terms unverified).
course_use: S3 demo of a vendor UI versus a notebook; check the free tier before class.

title: Sellforte
author_source: Sellforte, Espoo (Finland), 2017 to 2026, software and vendor (SaaS MMM, daily forecasts, incrementality tests, "agentic" media planner).
note: European SaaS MMM with public explainer content, including a page on Meridian and a note on data granularity; clients across Nordics and Baltics (Musti Group, Finnish Design Shop) give a multi-country angle.
course_use: Background; strong European guest-talk candidate (Helsinki, remote).

title: Analytic Partners (GPS Enterprise)
author_source: Analytic Partners, New York with European offices, 1999 to 2026, software and vendor (GPS-Enterprise platform, ROI Genome benchmarks; Gartner MMM leader).
note: The large-enterprise "commercial analytics" model: data ingestion to optimisation, cross-market benchmarks (ROI Genome). Useful for discussing what enterprises buy versus what open source gives.
course_use: Background; S3 vendor landscape.

title: Nielsen MMM (now Circana)
author_source: Nielsen, then Circana (acquisition completed 21 August 2025), vendor and report. Nielsen "Marketing Mix Modeling Best Practices" guide, 2022.
note: Decades of multi-country MMM practice; the best-practices PDF is a short, readable client-side checklist (granularity, data requirements). Note the ownership change when citing.
course_use: S1 or background reading.

title: Ipsos MMA
author_source: Ipsos MMA, 1990s to 2026, vendor (unified marketing measurement; Gartner MMM Magic Quadrant leader 2024 and 2025).
note: Clear statement of "unified measurement" (MMM plus attribution plus tests in one framework), the vendor positioning students will meet in practice.
course_use: S5 reading on triangulation; background.

title: Measured
author_source: Measured, 2017 to 2026, software and vendor (incrementality testing platform with test-calibrated MMM; pricing reported from about USD 50k per year).
note: Good public FAQ material on when to use incrementality tests, attribution or MMM, and ten real-world MMM examples.
course_use: S5 reading; background.

title: Haus
author_source: Haus, 2021 to 2026, software and vendor (geo incrementality experiments, "causal MMM"; USD 55m funding to 2025).
note: Their "Incrementality 101" and geo-experiment fundamentals posts are short, well written primers on design, power and synthetic control in business language.
course_use: S5 pre-reading for the geo-experiment session.

title: Lifesight
author_source: Lifesight, Singapore and US, 2016 to 2026, software and vendor (no-code causal MMM, incrementality, attribution). Maintains the CC0 "awesome-marketing-measurement" list on GitHub.
note: The awesome list (15 sections: open-source MMM, geo experiments, attribution, datasets, papers, courses, communities) is a handy vendor-neutral index for students. Lifesight announced an open-source forecasting engine "Horizon" but no repository was visible on their GitHub organisation (unverified).
course_use: Background; give students the awesome list in week 1.

title: MASS Analytics (MassTer)
author_source: MASS Analytics (Dr Ramla Jarrar), London and Tunis, 2010s to 2026, software and vendor (MassTer MMM desktop software, Bayesian and hierarchical options; MMM Academy).
note: One of the few vendors that packages teaching with the tool: free YouTube course, paid academy with certificate and software access, 2-week MassTer trial licences with their Udemy course. Listed price about GBP 12,000 per year; no formal academic licence found, worth asking.
course_use: S2 reading (free course videos); vendor demo candidate. Trial licence free for two weeks.

title: Ekimetrics (Eki.Decisions)
author_source: Ekimetrics, Paris (offices in London, New York, Dubai), 2006 to 2026, vendor and consultancy (MMM core with modules; Gartner "Visionary" 2025; Meta and TikTok measurement partner).
note: European leader in multi-market MMM for FMCG and luxury; co-author of the Artefact and Meta Robyn comparison study. Their "Bayesian MMM with limited data" style posts are useful for small-country models.
course_use: Background; European guest-talk candidate (Paris).

title: Keen Decision Systems
author_source: Keen, Durham NC, 2010 to 2026, software and vendor (adaptive Bayesian MMM with real-time scenario planning).
note: Announced a free-access MMM programme (scope unverified); a mid-market example of self-serve forecasting and planning.
course_use: Background; check the free-access terms for a student exercise.

title: Artefact
author_source: Artefact, Paris, 2015 to 2026, consultancy and vendor (Google Meridian certified; custom hierarchical Bayesian and graphical causal MMM; Robyn versus GCM study with Meta on five international FMCG brands).
note: Shows how consultancies build on open-source engines and where they add causal structure (DAGs). The five-brand international comparison is directly relevant.
course_use: S2 or S5 reading; European guest-talk candidate.

title: OLS and log-log (constant elasticity) response models
author_source: Hanssens, Parsons and Schultz, 2001, book (Market Response Models, 2nd ed., Springer, chapters on functional forms); Tellis, 2006, book chapter ("Modeling Marketing Mix", Handbook of Marketing Research, Sage).
note: Defines the linear, multiplicative (log-log) and semi-log forms, elasticities and the economics behind them; Tellis is the compact 17-page primer.
course_use: S1 reading; statsmodels lab. Paywalled (library access).

title: Adstock variants (geometric, delayed, Weibull)
author_source: Jin, Wang, Sun, Chan and Koehler, 2017, paper (Google Research technical report); Robyn documentation, "Key features" (geometric and Weibull adstock).
note: Jin et al. formalise carryover (geometric and delayed adstock) and shape effects in one Bayesian model; Robyn's docs explain the Weibull PDF and CDF variants used in practice.
course_use: S2 core reading.

title: Hill and logistic saturation
author_source: Jin et al., 2017 (as above, Hill shape function); Google Meridian documentation, "Media saturation and lagging".
note: Hill(x; ec, slope) with half-saturation point and slope is now the default in Meridian and Robyn; the docs show how it interacts with adstock and why the two are hard to separate.
course_use: S2 lab (plot response curves, derive marginal ROI).

title: Ridge regression with hyperparameter search (Robyn approach)
author_source: Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, 2009, book (Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., section 3.4 shrinkage methods, free PDF); Zhou et al., 2024, paper ("Packaging Up Media Mix Modeling: An Introduction to Robyn's Open-Source Approach", arXiv 2403.14674 and MSI working paper).
note: ESL gives the L2 penalty and bias-variance trade-off; the Robyn paper documents the Nevergrad multi-objective search over adstock, Hill and lambda and the model-selection criteria.
course_use: S2 reading; compare with Bayesian priors.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (geo-level MMM)
author_source: Sun, Wang, Jin, Chan and Koehler, 2017, paper (Geo-level Bayesian Hierarchical Media Mix Modeling, Google); Wang, Jin, Sun, Chan and Koehler, 2017, paper (hierarchical approach using category data).
note: The basis of Meridian: sub-national or multi-country units share priors, which tightens credible intervals and protects against unsound reallocation. The category paper shows how to borrow strength across brands or markets via informative priors.
course_use: S3 core reading for cross-country allocation.

title: Time-varying coefficients and Gaussian processes
author_source: Ng, Wang and Dai, 2021, paper (Bayesian Time Varying Coefficient Model with Applications to MMM, AdKDD 2021, arXiv 2106.03322); PyMC-Marketing notebook "MMM with time-varying parameters" (HSGP); Rasmussen and Williams, 2006, book (GPML, free PDF).
note: Media effectiveness drifts; KTR (Orbit) and HSGP (PyMC-Marketing) are the two practical ways to let coefficients or baselines move smoothly over time.
course_use: S2 advanced demo; S4 link to forecasting.

title: Fourier seasonality
author_source: Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, 2021, book (Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd ed., chapter 7 "Time series regression models", section on Fourier terms, free online); Taylor and Letham, 2018, article (Forecasting at Scale, The American Statistician 72(1), 37 to 45).
note: Fourier pairs are how Prophet, PyMC-Marketing and Meridian represent yearly seasonality with few parameters; fpp3 explains the choice of K.
course_use: S2 and S4.

title: Panel fixed effects and partial pooling
author_source: Gelman and Hill, 2007, book (Data Analysis Using Regression and Multilevel/Hierarchical Models, Cambridge, chapter 12 on partial pooling); linearmodels documentation (PanelOLS fixed effects).
note: Makes the link between country fixed effects (no pooling), pooled OLS (complete pooling) and hierarchical priors (partial pooling), which is the central modelling decision in a multi-country MMM.
course_use: S3 reading and lab. Gelman and Hill is paywalled; chapter 12 circulates as a PDF in many course sites.

title: Budget optimisation under constraints
author_source: PyMC-Marketing notebook "Budget Allocation with PyMC-Marketing" (SLSQP with bounds and custom constraints, plus risk assessment and multi-objective variants); Google Meridian docs "Budget optimization scenarios" (fixed versus flexible budget, minimal marginal ROI or target ROI constraints).
note: Both docs show the same mathematics (maximise expected response subject to total budget and per-channel bounds) in code students can run, including uncertainty in the optimum.
course_use: S3 lab (allocate across countries and channels with floor and cap constraints).

title: Forecasting with ETS, ARIMA and regression
author_source: Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, 2021, book (fpp3 chapters 8 "Exponential smoothing", 9 "ARIMA models", 10 "Dynamic regression models"); StatsForecast documentation.
note: The standard, free text; dynamic regression (ARIMA errors with media regressors) is the bridge between forecasting and MMM.
course_use: S4 core reading and lab.

title: Difference-in-differences
author_source: Roth, Sant'Anna, Bilinski and Poe, 2023, article (What's trending in difference-in-differences? Journal of Econometrics 235(2), 2218 to 2244); CausalPy documentation.
note: Synthesises staggered adoption, parallel-trends violations and inference, with practitioner recommendations; CausalPy implements standard and staggered DiD.
course_use: S5 reading and lab.

title: Synthetic control
author_source: Abadie, 2021, article (Using Synthetic Controls: Feasibility, Data Requirements, and Methodological Aspects, Journal of Economic Literature 59(2), 391 to 425, open access); Brodersen et al., 2015, article (CausalImpact, Annals of Applied Statistics 9(1), 247 to 274).
note: Abadie is the definitive guide to when synthetic control is credible (donor pool, pre-period fit, placebo tests); Brodersen gives the Bayesian state-space version used in CausalImpact.
course_use: S5 reading; CausalPy and tfcausalimpact labs.

title: Geo experiments and power
author_source: Vaver and Koehler, 2011, paper (Measuring Ad Effectiveness Using Geo Experiments, Google); Chen and Au, 2022, article (Robust causal inference for incremental return on ad spend with randomized paired geo experiments, Annals of Applied Statistics 16(1); Trimmed Match, arXiv 1908.02922) and Trimmed Match Design (arXiv 2105.07060).
note: Vaver and Koehler is the original geo-based regression design; Trimmed Match adds robust paired designs and power-based pair selection. GeoLift's power tools and Haus's primers build on both.
course_use: S5 core reading; power-calculation exercise with GeoLift or Trimmed Match.

title: Logistic (data-driven) attribution
author_source: Shao and Li, 2011, paper (Data-driven multi-touch attribution models, KDD 2011, pages 258 to 264).
note: The first data-driven MTA: bagged logistic regression on touchpoint exposure plus a probabilistic second-order model for credit assignment; the reference point for all later MTA work.
course_use: S5 reading. ACM paywall (library access).

title: Shapley value attribution
author_source: Zhao, Mahboobi and Bagheri, 2018, paper (Shapley Value Methods for Attribution Modeling in Online Advertising, arXiv 1804.05327).
note: Clear derivation of ordered and unordered Shapley attribution with an efficient computation; the method behind Google Analytics' former data-driven attribution.
course_use: S5 lab (compute Shapley credit on a synthetic journey dataset). Free.

title: Markov chain attribution
author_source: Anderl, Becker, von Wangenheim and Schumann, 2016, article (Mapping the customer journey: Lessons learned from graph-based online attribution modeling, International Journal of Research in Marketing 33(3), 457 to 474).
note: The removal-effect Markov attribution framework, from a German research team (Passau and ETH), with first- and higher-order chains and spillover findings; the basis of the R ChannelAttribution package.
