course_use: S5 reading. Elsevier paywall (WU library).

title: Calibration with lift tests
author_source: Zhang, Wurm, Li, Wakim, Kelly, Price and Liu, 2024, paper (Media Mix Model Calibration With Bayesian Priors, Google Research); PyMC-Marketing notebooks "Lift test calibration" and "Mitigating unobserved confounders with lift test likelihoods".
note: Reparametrising channel effects as ROI and placing experiment-informed priors on them is now the industry standard (Meridian ROI priors, Robyn calibration); the PyMC-Marketing notebooks show it in code with simulated confounding.
course_use: S5 lab linking experiments back into the MMM.

title: Identifiability and multicollinearity diagnostics
author_source: Chan and Perry, 2017, paper (Challenges and Opportunities in Media Mix Modeling, Google); Chen, Chan, Perry, Jin, Sun, Wang and Koehler, 2018, paper (Bias Correction for Paid Search in Media Mix Modeling, arXiv 1807.03292); statsmodels VIF.
note: Chan and Perry list the structural problems (collinear spend, selection bias, limited variation, ad-hoc functional forms); the paid-search paper gives a back-door correction. Together with VIF and prior-posterior checks they are the honest "what can this model not tell you" session.
course_use: S2 reading and a diagnostics checklist students apply to their own model.

title: Google Meridian simulated geo-level data
author_source: Google, 2025, dataset in the Meridian repo; Apache 2.0
note: 6,240 rows: 40 geos x 156 weeks (25 January 2021 to 15 January 2024), 5 paid channels with impressions and spend, 1 organic channel, 2 controls, promo flag, conversions, revenue per conversion and population (20 columns, about 1 MB). Sibling files add reach and frequency, national-level and a "hypothetical" future scenario for budget optimisation.
course_use: Session 3 lab alternative (hierarchical geo model and allocation); the geos can be relabelled as countries.

title: PyMC-Marketing example data (mmm_example.csv)
author_source: PyMC Labs, 2023 onward, dataset in the pymc-marketing repo; Apache 2.0
note: 179 weekly rows (2 April 2018 to 30 August 2021), 2 media channels, 2 event dummies, trend and seasonality helpers (8 columns, 12 KB). Tiny, so sampling is fast; matches the library's own tutorial.
course_use: Session 2 warm-up before the Alpenglow Germany data.

title: Robyn demo data (dt_simulated_weekly)
author_source: Meta Marketing Science, 2021 onward, dataset shipped with Robyn (R and Python); MIT
note: 208 weekly rows (23 November 2015 to 11 November 2019), 12 columns: revenue, TV, OOH, print, Facebook (impressions and spend), search (clicks and spend), competitor sales, events, newsletter. The most widely used MMM demo, so students can compare their Python results with countless Robyn write-ups.
course_use: Session 2 lab or exercise (reproduce a Robyn-style decomposition in PyMC-Marketing).

title: Synthetic benchmark with endogenous marketing spend
author_source: arXiv 2608.21130, 2026, paper plus seeded generator and reference instance with notebooks; licence stated in the repository (unverified)
note: Unlike Robyn and Meridian simulations, spend here reacts to seasons, promotions and past performance, so it tests whether a model survives endogeneity; ground truth is known.
course_use: Session 3 or 5 stretch exercise: fit the course model and check recovery of true ROAS.

title: siMMMulator and PySiMMMulator (simulation packages)
author_source: Meta Marketing Science (R, MIT, author Jessica Nguyen) and PySiMMMulator (Python port, PyPI 0.6.2, 2024, Ryan Duecker); software
note: Generate MMM data from first principles (baseline, spend, impressions, conversions) with user-chosen true ROI, so students can make their own ground-truth tests.
course_use: Session 5 project option: build a simulator for a seventh market.

title: Meta GeoLift sample data
author_source: Meta, 2021 onward, datasets in the GeoLift R package (GeoLift_PreTest, GeoLift_Test, GeoLift_Test_MultiCell); MIT
note: Daily sales by location for pre-test and test periods, built for synthetic-control geo experiments; the pre-test file is the standard power-analysis example.
course_use: Session 4 geo-lift lab (load the .rda files with pyreadr).

title: Kaggle: Sample Media Spends Data
author_source: Kaggle user yugagrawal95, dataset; licence not visible from here (unverified)
note: 3,051 rows, 9 columns, 113 weeks (January 2018 to February 2020), 8 digital channels (Facebook, Google search, email, YouTube, affiliate and more) plus sales; channel-week long format is good practice for reshaping.
course_use: Session 2 exercise; requires a Kaggle account.

title: Kaggle: MMM demo dataset (bike sales)
author_source: Kaggle user mattwalentosky, dataset; licence not visible from here (unverified)
note: Five years of fictitious weekly bike sales driven by Google Trends plus marketing spend; useful for showing how a search-interest covariate can absorb media effects.
course_use: Session 4 forecasting exercise.

title: Dunnhumby: The Complete Journey and Breakfast at the Frat
author_source: dunnhumby Source Files, retail transaction and promotion datasets; free download under dunnhumby terms (non-commercial; permission needed to publish results, per search summary; unverified)
note: Complete Journey: 2,500 households over two years with transactions, coupons and campaigns. Breakfast at the Frat: 156 weeks of store-product sales with base price, shelf price and display/feature flags across four categories, the cleanest free data for price and promotion elasticities.
course_use: Session 1 elasticity lab (Breakfast at the Frat); Session 4 attribution background.

title: Dominick's Finer Foods scanner data
author_source: Kilts Center, Chicago Booth, store-level weekly scanner data 1989 to 1997; free for academic use with registration. Eurostat's cleaned version and code: EUPL 1.2
note: About 100 million observations, 18,000 UPCs, 29 categories, 90+ stores, almost 400 weeks; the classic for store-level price response and a reasonable stand-in for a "geo" panel.
course_use: Session 1 or 3 (treat stores as geos); subset one category before class.

title: NielsenIQ via the Kilts Center (Consumer Panel, Retail Scanner, Ad Intel)
author_source: Kilts Center, Chicago Booth; academic subscription, US data only
note: Weekly retail scanner data since 2006 from 90+ chains plus advertising occurrences by media type: the only large public-to-academics source that combines sales and advertising.
course_use: Background and thesis work only. Cost USD 3,000 for three years for one dataset (faculty subscription; up to two PhD students free); not usable for a 30-student class.

title: Google Trends
author_source: Google, ongoing; web tool and unofficial Python access (pytrends)
note: Free weekly search-interest indices by country, the standard proxy for demand and for organic interest in all six Alpenglow markets; index values (0 to 100) are relative, not volumes.
course_use: Session 3 and 4 covariate; mind rate limits and the terms of service.

title: Eurostat
author_source: European Commission, ongoing; database and API (Python package eurostat); CC BY 4.0
note: Monthly HICP, retail trade volume, consumer confidence and unemployment for AT, DE, FR, IT, NL, PL; the natural macro controls for a cross-country MMM and the source for PPP price-level adjustments.
course_use: Session 3 (controls and price-level normalisation).

title: World Bank World Development Indicators
author_source: World Bank, ongoing; API (Python package wbgapi); CC BY 4.0
note: Annual GDP per capita, PPP conversion factors, population and internet penetration for every country; needed when extending the model to emerging markets or scaling spend across currencies.
course_use: Session 3 and 5 (emerging-market extension in projects).

title: Juan Camilo Orduz
author_source: VP Marketing Analytics, PyMC Labs; Berlin; person (core author of PyMC-Marketing's MMM module)
note: Writes the most detailed public worked examples of Bayesian MMM, hierarchical geo models and lift-test calibration in Python; his notebooks are the closest public analogue to Session 3's lab.
course_use: Session 3 background reading; strong remote guest-talk candidate (Berlin, same time zone) on calibrating an MMM with experiments.

title: Thomas Wiecki
author_source: CEO and co-founder, PyMC Labs; co-author of PyMC; Berlin area; person
note: The public voice of Bayesian MMM; frequent posts on priors, identifiability and why Bayesian beats ridge for MMM; case studies with HelloFresh and Bolt.
course_use: Session 2-3 motivation; guest-talk candidate (vendor and open-source angle), realistic by video.

title: Gufeng Zhou
author_source: Marketing Science, Meta; creator of Robyn; London; person
note: Author of the most used open-source MMM in industry; his Medium and LinkedIn pieces on experiment calibration explain Robyn's design choices (ridge, Nevergrad, calibration).
course_use: Session 2 (Robyn as the R and ridge benchmark); vendor-side guest talk angle (Meta Marketing Science Europe).

title: Google Meridian team
author_source: Google Meridian Marketing Mix Modeling Team (the README cites the team, not individuals); person/team
note: Meridian is the reference implementation of geo-level hierarchical Bayesian MMM with reach and frequency, exactly the structure used in Session 3; their docs on geo selection are directly reusable.
course_use: Session 3 (geo hierarchy); follow via the GitHub repo and the Think with Google measurement pages. No single named person to follow; see JSM 2025 talk "Meridian: Google's Open-Source Marketing Mix Model" (https://ww2.amstat.org/meetings/jsm/2025/onlineprogram/abstract.cfm?sid=2361&tid=2363, unverified).

title: Harald van Heerde
author_source: Research Professor of Marketing, UNSW Sydney; Fellow, Tilburg University; person
note: Leading author on promotion response, decomposition of sales lifts, and marketing effectiveness across business cycles; essential for the baseline vs incremental logic.
course_use: Session 2 background (promotion decomposition), Session 1 elasticities.

title: Marnik Dekimpe
author_source: Research Professor of Marketing, Tilburg University, and Professor, KU Leuven; person
note: Persistence modelling and long-run effects; cross-country work on private labels and retail in Europe fits the international angle.
course_use: Session 3 background (cross-country heterogeneity); realistic academic guest from the Benelux.

title: Peter Danaher
author_source: Professor of Marketing and Econometrics, Monash University; Melbourne; person
note: Media exposure, reach and frequency modelling and multichannel attribution with field tests; directly relevant to Meridian's reach and frequency extension.
course_use: Session 4 attribution background.

title: Jan-Benedict Steenkamp
author_source: C. Knox Massey Distinguished Professor of Marketing, UNC Kenan-Flagler; Editor in Chief, Journal of Marketing; person
note: The international marketing reference (global brands, emerging markets, private label); frames why effects differ across the six Alpenglow markets.
course_use: Session 3 (cross-country) and Session 5 framing.

title: Raoul Kübler
author_source: Professor of Marketing, ESSEC Business School; Cergy/Paris; German, previously Münster; person
note: Co-author of "Applied Marketing Analytics Using R" (SAGE, with Yildirim), teaches MMM hands-on; posts on how MMM results get manipulated are perfect critical-thinking material.
course_use: Session 2 reading; realistic academic guest speaker (German speaker, European time zone, teaches exactly this material).

title: Gokhan Yildirim
author_source: Associate Professor of Marketing, Imperial College Business School; London; person
note: MMM and multichannel budget allocation research (direct mail vs email field tests, JAMS 2023); co-author of the applied R textbook.
course_use: Session 3 budget allocation background.

title: Nicolas Padilla
author_source: Assistant Professor of Marketing, London Business School; person
note: Works explicitly on "modern marketing mix models" with first-party data and machine learning; one of few academics engaging with the Bayesian MMM revival.
course_use: Session 3 background; remote guest candidate (London).

title: Bernd Skiera
author_source: Professor, Chair of Electronic Commerce, Goethe University Frankfurt; person
note: Online advertising economics, attribution, and the GDPR tracking study (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.06862); the German-speaking reference on why attribution breaks and MMM returns.
course_use: Session 4 attribution; realistic guest (Frankfurt, two hours from Vienna by air).

title: Christian Schulze
author_source: Associate Professor of Marketing, Frankfurt School of Finance and Management; person
note: Digital marketing and customer analytics with a strong quantitative bent; co-author with Skiera on marketing ROI and attribution.
course_use: Session 4 background; Frankfurt-based guest candidate.

title: Martin Spann
author_source: Professor and Director, Institute of Electronic Commerce and Digital Markets, LMU Munich; person
note: Pricing, mobile and digital markets; useful for the price elasticity and digital channel parts.
course_use: Session 1 background; Munich guest candidate.

title: Mike Taylor
author_source: Independent, co-founder of Ladder (marketing agency), author; London; person
note: Practitioner tutorials comparing Robyn, LightweightMMM and PyMC-Marketing from a marketer's view; also writes on AI-assisted analysis, matching the course's AI-coding approach.
course_use: Session 2 optional reading.

title: Eric Seufert
author_source: Heracles Media, author of Mobile Dev Memo; person
note: Explains the privacy-driven revival of MMM (ATT, cookie loss) better than anyone; good for the "why now" argument.
course_use: Session 1 motivation.

title: Jim Gianoglio
author_source: Founder, Cauzle Analytics and MMM Hub; USA; person
note: Runs the MMM Hub newsletter, Slack and podcast; curates practically every new MMM resource. Marketing Analytics Summit talk "Cracking the Code: Mastering Modern MMM" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FEG-Vtj7Y9Q
course_use: Point students to MMM Hub in Session 1; the YouTube talk is a 40-minute overview for Session 2.

title: Kevin Hartman
author_source: Director of Analytics, Google; author of "Digital Marketing Analytics: In Theory and in Practice"; person
note: Accessible textbook framing of measurement choices; useful for students without a statistics background.
course_use: Background.

title: Dominik Papies
author_source: Professor of Marketing, University of Tübingen; person
note: Market response models and the standard reference chapter on endogeneity in marketing models; exactly the "why is media spend endogenous" problem in Session 2 and 3.
course_use: Session 2 reading on endogeneity; German guest candidate.

title: Jochen Hartmann
author_source: Professor of Digital Marketing, TUM School of Management, Munich; person
note: Generative AI, multimodal ad analytics and unstructured data; complements MMM with creative-quality covariates.
course_use: Session 4 or 5 extension; Munich guest candidate.

title: Thomas Reutterer, WU Vienna
author_source: Professor of Marketing, Head of Institute for Marketing and Customer Analytics, WU Vienna; academic
note: In-house WU colleague with a long record in marketing analytics and Bayesian methods; zero travel cost.

title: Nils Wlömert and Nadia Abou Nabout, WU Vienna
author_source: Professors, Retailing and Data Science (Wlömert) and AI in Marketing Analytics (Abou Nabout), WU Department of Marketing; academic
note: Abou Nabout works on online advertising auctions and attribution, Wlömert on retail data science; both are on campus.

title: Analytic Partners, Hamburg and Munich
author_source: Analytic Partners GmbH (Gartner MMM Magic Quadrant leader 2025); Hamburg office opened 2017 under Achim Schoeneich (Managing Director Germany, role as of 2017); vendor

title: Adtriba (now part of Funnel), Hamburg
author_source: János Moldvay, founder and CEO, Adtriba; acquired by Funnel in 2024; vendor

title: Nexoya, Zurich

note: Regression-based cross-channel attribution and automated budget reallocation for brands such as Zurich Insurance, Generali, Swisscom; a Swiss example of operationalised allocation.

title: dentsu Austria and Merkle, Vienna
author_source: dentsu Austria GmbH, Vienna; Merkle (dentsu) runs a Marketing Measurement and Optimisation practice and is a Google Meridian partner (partner status unverified); agency
note: Network agency with a Vienna office and a Meridian-based measurement practice in the group.

title: GroupM Austria (WPP), Vienna
author_source: GroupM Austria, about 350 staff in Vienna; agency
note: WPP's media investment arm; GroupM's global analytics units (Choreograph, [m]Science) run MMM for Austrian clients.

title: e-dialog, Vienna
